title: What happens if you fall into a black hole

beats.vo: To anyone far away, you'd freeze at the edge.
beats.visual: Near-black. A lone astronaut in a white suit hangs in front of a glowing orange ring of light, rim-lit by hard Horizon-orange. Hard push-in toward the figure; the figure's motion visibly stalls mid-reach. Reads in under 2 s.

beats.vo: Friends far away would watch you slow down. Then stop, just short of the edge.
beats.visual: Cut to a distant, tiny observer on a dark ledge, watching through a lens flare. Locked-off long lens; the astronaut's motion in the far frame decelerates like a film frame-rate dropping to a hold.

beats.vo: That edge is the event horizon. Point of no return. Not even light escapes.
beats.visual: Camera follows a streak of light curving into the black disc and vanishing at a razor-thin edge. Hard orange rim light on the edge; a thin Anton label fades in. Camera tracks the light (follow).

beats.vo: Why? Gravity bends space and time so hard, your picture slows to a stop.
beats.visual: Starfield behind the disc warps into arcs and double images. Slow lateral slide so the stars stretch past the lens, then the astronaut's image smears and holds.

beats.vo: On your own clock, NASA's simulation says, the fall takes about three hours.
beats.visual: Over-the-shoulder behind the astronaut, accretion disc glowing to the side, a wrist clock in sharp foreground focus ticking steadily. Slow push toward the horizon; hold steady so the clock reads as normal.
beats.tts: On your own clock, NASA's simulation says the fall takes about three hours.

beats.vo: A giant black hole, about four million Suns. Like the one in our galaxy's center.
beats.visual: Reveal pull-back: the astronaut shrinks to a speck against the huge disc, a tiny Sun-yellow dot for scale in the corner. Pull-back reveals the scale.

beats.vo: Cross the edge, and space itself rushes inward at light speed.
screen: space flows inward at light speed
beats.visual: Camera tracks with the astronaut across the edge; streaks of starlight all rush inward toward one point. Light falls, camera leads the way in.

beats.vo: Then the simulation gives you twelve point eight seconds, before you're torn apart.
beats.visual: Anton countdown 12.8 slams in, Horizon orange, over the dark inner view; the numerals tick down on the beat. Push-in on the number.
beats.tts: Then the simulation gives you twelve point eight seconds before you're torn apart.

beats.vo: The closer end of you gets pulled harder. You stretch like a noodle.
beats.visual: Side view: the astronaut silhouette, rim lit, is pulled lengthwise toward a point, thin and long. Slow lateral dolly beside the stretching figure.
Condensed word SPAGHETTIFICATION slams in with a sub hit; letters stretch vertically. Hold 1 s.

beats.vo: A small black hole is worse. It can tear you apart before the edge.
beats.visual: Split frame: left a giant black hole with a calm approach, right a small tight black hole where the figure breaks apart well before the edge. Impact shake allowed on the tear.

beats.vo: At the center, math says a point of endless crush. Nobody knows if it's real.
beats.visual: Dark centre; a single pinprick of violet light. Slow push-in to the pin; a question mark resolves in Ultraviolet.

beats.vo: Nothing from inside can reach us. This is math, not a memory.
beats.visual: Slow pull-back from the stamp to the empty dark ring with a single faint photon ring. Calm, no shake.

screen: CLAIM: you'd freeze at the edge
beats.visual: Signature stamp: CASE FILE 002 header, a big Anton UNPROVEN stamp slams down in Ultraviolet on Abyss. Deep hit. Hold 1 s still.

beats.vo: To anyone far away, you'd freeze at the edge. To you, you'd fall right through.
beats.visual: Split frame holds: left the frozen astronaut at the rim, right the same astronaut sliding through, both rim-lit orange. Slow push-in on the join, end on the rule card for about 1 s.

end_card.text: Case file 002 · UNPROVEN · Nothing from inside can reach us. This is math, not a memory.
